audit_findings.title: Recurring fleet-capital recoveries may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $634 million of gross FY2025 cash recoveries at issue ($468 million equipment-sale proceeds plus $166 million sales-type lease collections); net correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential omission from owner earnings of recurring cash recovered when fleet and sales-type lease capital is realized.
audit_findings.evidence: We consider total cash generated and free cash flow to be important measures of comparative operating performance, as our principal sources of operating liquidity are cash from operations and proceeds from the sale of revenue earning equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated omission. The filed gross recoveries exceed the negative $339.6 million anchor by $294.4 million, so excluding a substantial nonduplicative portion could change both the anchor's sign and the valuation conclusion. The $166 million collections may already be embedded in operating cash flow, and sale gains already recognized in earnings must not be counted twice.
audit_findings.action: Bridge FY2025 OE line by line to the cash-flow statement, separately identifying the $468 million sale proceeds, $166 million lease collections, related book values, gains or losses already in earnings, and any amounts already included through operating cash flow; then rerun all scenarios using only the nonduplicative correction.

audit_findings.title: Gross capital expenditure may have been mistaken for maintenance capital expenditure
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.055 billion of FY2025 gross capital expenditures is subject to classification; actual maintenance-capex correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Owner earnings deducts maintenance capital expenditure; treating replacement and customer-backed growth investment as maintenance reduces OE and its DCF value.
audit_findings.evidence: The level of capital required to support the ChoiceLease product line varies based on customer contract signings for replacement vehicles and growth.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved classification possibility. The filing shows $1.508 billion of ChoiceLease spending, $311 million of rental spending, and $236 million of operating-property spending, but it does not establish that all $2.055 billion was maintenance. Reclassifying only $339.6 million, or 16.5% of gross capex, would eliminate the negative anchor, so the issue is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 additions by replacement, signed-contract growth, rental expansion, and operating-property maintenance using vehicle counts, retirements, disposals, contract signings, useful lives, and required capacity; rerun OE and every scenario with the evidenced maintenance amount.

audit_findings.title: A permanently negative anchor makes the scenario framework economically inverted
audit_findings.magnitude: Bull operating PV is $1.714 billion below bear and bull value is $41.78 per share below bear; FY2025 filed free cash flow was positive $946 million versus the negative $339.6 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth assumptions are applied directly to negative OE, causing higher nominal growth to compound losses and reverse the intended bull/base/bear ordering.
audit_findings.evidence: Free cash flow (a non-GAAP measure) increased to $946 million in 2025 from $133 million in 2024, primarily reflecting reduced capital expenditures and higher cash from operating activities.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated model-logic error: bear value is -$82.74 per share, base is -$110.95, and bull is -$124.52. The scenarios therefore do not express improving economic outcomes. The separate conflict with positive filed earnings, operating cash flow, and free cash flow does not by itself prove OE is wrong, but it makes reconciliation necessary before capitalizing the negative anchor into a perpetuity.
audit_findings.action: Produce a complete bridge from FY2025 filed earnings and cash flows to -$339.6 million OE. If normalized OE remains negative, retain the too-hard conclusion and replace the growth cases with an explicit recovery, runoff, or liquidation model; otherwise rerun the DCF from the reconciled normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: The share denominator includes unissued ESPP capacity rather than an existing common-equity claim
audit_findings.magnitude: 1.325873 million excess shares, or 3.23% of the 41.032336 million denominator; excluding them changes base value from -$110.95 to approximately -$114.64 per share, a $3.69 change
audit_findings.mechanism: Unused ESPP authorization inflates fully diluted shares without a corresponding equity claim or purchase proceeds; with negative equity value, this makes reported per-share value less negative.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, there were 7.5 million shares authorized for issuance and 1.3 million shares remaining available to be purchased in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated denominator error, but it does not change the valuation conclusion. Excluding the unused capacity produces approximately -$85.50 bear, -$114.64 base, and -$128.67 bull values, changes of only $2.76 to $4.15 per share, versus the $248.44 market price and a base valuation gap exceeding $359 per share.
audit_findings.action: Remove the 1.325873 million unused ESPP shares; rebuild dilution from 38.346868 million shares outstanding plus existing awards, probability-weighted performance awards, and in-the-money options, including exercise or purchase proceeds consistently and applying a sign-aware dilution rule.

audit_findings.title: Core sales-type lease interest could have been purged as portfolio income
audit_findings.magnitude: $90 million of FY2025 sales-type lease interest, equal to 26.5% of the absolute $339.6 million OE anchor; after-tax OE correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An operating-revenue item may have been removed by the portfolio-interest purge, lowering recurring OE while leaving the supporting lease capital within the business perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: We recognize revenue for sales-type leases using the effective interest method, which provides a constant periodic rate of return on the outstanding investment in the lease.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated purge. The filing identifies the $90 million as interest earned through Ryder's sales-type leasing operations. Its scale relative to the anchor is large enough to affect the DCF materially, although the net OE effect cannot be established without the purge schedule and applicable tax treatment.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the purge ledger by account and confirm whether the $90 million was retained. If removed, restore its evidenced after-tax operating amount, ensure related lease collections and capital are treated consistently, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The pension deficit is a senior claim not shown in the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $95 million FY2025 net funded deficit; a full incremental deduction equals approximately $2.32 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unfunded pension obligation not already captured through OE contributions or expense would be deducted as a senior claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the aggregate present value of obligations of our global defined pension plans was $1.6 billion, and the fair value of the plan assets of our global defined benefit pension plans was $1.5 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted presentation is real, but the maximum evidenced FY2025 adjustment is only 2.1% of the absolute $4.552 billion base equity value and less than 1% of the $248.44 market price per share. It cannot change the deeply negative valuation conclusion. The June 2026 filing reports pension and other employee-benefit liabilities together rather than an updated consolidated funded status, and double counting remains possible because pension expense and contributions pass through earnings or cash flow.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 plan-by-plan funded status and required contribution schedule; reconcile them to OE, including the $19 million Canadian settlement, and deduct only the residual economic deficit not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $62.3 million in FY2016, equal to 5.0% of filed FY2016 D&A; FY2025 amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible non-economic D&A left as an expense reduces historical or anchor OE and could affect normalization or growth assessment.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2016 $62.3m (5.0% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The conservative direction is established, but current materiality is not. The supplied amount concerns 2016, while the valuation uses FY2025 as its anchor; no FY2025 residual amount or component classification is provided. The record therefore cannot determine whether correcting this item would materially affect the current valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 filed D&A by asset class and economic function, identify any eligible non-economic residual, and rerun the anchor and scenarios only for amounts supported by filed evidence.
